_readme: Cards for draw.mjs. Two modes. AGENCY (default): professional levers — quality references, composition systems, brand devices, palette strategies, type strategies; the brand hue is sampled separately. EXPRESSIVE (opt-in): medium/constraint/twist/palette cards from non-screen visual traditions. Never add the AI-tasteful clichés (Swiss style, brutalism, broadsheet, CRT/terminal, Bauhaus, risograph, Y2K, vaporwave, bento) and never name a specific website to imitate.
medium: ferry timetable pinned in a harbour office
constraint: No cards anywhere: content never sits in boxed tiles
Type only: zero images or illustrations above the fold
Exactly two inks plus the paper colour
Navigation IS the hero: the first screen is the index of the site
One font size for all body and UI text; hierarchy only through weight, position, and colour
A single vertical axis at the left third; everything hangs off it
The main content is a real table: rows, columns, sortable if it helps
One enormous element per viewport, everything else small
Nothing is centred, anywhere, ever
No borders or rules: separation only through colour fields and space
Every section has a different ground colour drawn from the palette
The grid is visible and part of the design
The hero has no headline: it opens with the thing itself
Controls look like the subject's physical controls
Colour comes only from photography; UI chrome is monochrome
Maximum three type sizes on the whole site
Information density of a timetable: small type, lots of it, perfectly ordered
Huge margins, small text, lots of air
The subject's units of measure are the layout structure (rows = hours, columns = sizes, etc.)
One typeface family for everything
Footnotes and marginalia carry secondary content
Content reads as a form someone fills in
Asymmetric two-column split that changes ratio per section
Images are cropped into one shape taken from the subject
Motion only on user action: nothing animates on load
One horizontal-scroll band in an otherwise vertical page
Everything left-aligned and ragged; no justified or centred blocks
Dark ground that is a real-world colour (not near-black): oxblood, bottle green, navy ink, graphite slate
Light ground that is NOT cream or off-white: a saturated or mid-tone paper
The footer is the most designed part of the page
twist: The cursor or focus ring becomes a tool from the subject's world
Scroll progress is shown in the subject's own unit
Interactions leave a mark: a stamp, punch, tick, or ink trace
Numbers are set in a custom tabular style that becomes the identity
A running index or legend that tracks where you are
The primary action is a physical-object metaphor (tear-off, toggle, lever, dial)
The page has a 'back side' you can flip to
Hovering reveals an annotation layer, like a teacher's red pen or an engineer's markup
Dates and times are rendered in the subject's own format
A printed-receipt or ticket summary of what the visitor did
An interactive specimen: the visitor can manipulate the subject itself
Content is sorted and coded like the subject's own catalogue system
A single hand-drawn line or mark threads through the whole page
Section transitions borrow the subject's real-world transitions (pages turning, tide rising, gears)
The logo or wordmark is built from the subject's notation system
A live data element from the subject: today's tide, current queue, stock on hand
Sound-free 'audio' cues: visual metronome, VU-meter, rhythmic layout
Image captions written like museum or field-guide labels
A deliberate imperfection: misregistration, a stamp at an angle, hand-corrected typo
The 404 and empty states are the subject's equivalent (a lost ticket, an empty shelf)
palette: rust and verdigris on galvanised grey
kraft paper, black ink, safety orange
hospital mint, steel, and a red cross
maritime signal flags (primary red, yellow, blue)
racing green and putty-grey card stock
beekeeper's honey, wax, and smoke grey
copper sulfate blue and lab-glass clear
pine forest, bark, and trail-marker red
swimming-pool chlorine blue and tile grout
mimeograph purple-blue ink on newsprint grey (use as ink, not gradient)
bruise-blue night shift and fluorescent-tube white

the confidence of a luxury car maker's configurator
the calm clarity of a premium airline's booking flow
the pacing of a serious quarterly business magazine
the precision of an architecture firm's monograph
the warmth of a family-owned hotel group's brochure
the authority of a top-tier law firm's printed capabilities book
the polish of a flagship watchmaker's product page
the directness of a great engineering firm's project sheet
the composure of a museum's exhibition wayfinding
the editorial voice of an independent investment letter
the tactile quality of a premium stationery maker's catalogue
the orderliness of a world-class hospital's patient guide
the energy of a sports federation's season launch
the rigour of a central bank's data publication
the hospitality of a great restaurant group's menu design
the trustworthiness of a mutual insurer's member report
the craftsmanship of an outdoor-equipment maker's field guide
the clarity of a public transit authority's network map
the understatement of a consulting partnership's partner bios
composition: Typographic statement hero locked to a strict baseline grid, proof directly beneath, generous negative space
Full-bleed art-directed image hero with headline set into the image's quiet area
Product shown at heroic scale, cropped off-canvas, with a short claim and one action
Split composition with a persistent visual column while the narrative scrolls beside it
Sticky narrative: one evolving visual that changes state as each beat scrolls past
Index-led hero: the offer presented as a short, beautifully set table of contents
Asymmetric 7/5 grid throughout, with type hanging from a strong left axis
Large data-led hero: one real, sourced figure set huge, explained in a sentence
Layered depth: foreground type over a slow-moving background plane, no gradients
Column-based storytelling: three narrow editorial columns that widen as the page progresses
Statement band + case-study-led page: the work itself is the proof and the design
Quiet hero with a single detail photograph and a long, confident headline
Interactive product preview as the hero, framed by nothing but space
Horizontal chapters: each beat is a full-width band with its own ground colour
Modular page built from a single repeating proportion (e.g. 3:2 tiles in a strict system)
Conventional, impeccably executed: classic hero + proof + offer + people + ask, made exceptional purely by type, spacing and art direction
Card system done properly: a set of genuinely object-like items (cases, products, people) in a precise, varied grid
brand_device: a cropped fragment of the logomark used as a recurring graphic
a single precise line that threads through sections as a guide
a signature crop ratio and corner treatment applied to every image
a colour field that shifts tone section by section
a typographic numeral system for every figure on the site
masked text reveals as the only motion signature
a recurring frame or bracket shape drawn from the logo
a consistent caption system with small, precise type under every visual
an underline treatment for links and highlights unique to the brand
a pattern built from the brand's initial, used at very low contrast
a grid of fine rules as structure, revealed only at key moments
a distinctive hover behaviour shared by every interactive element
a monogram seal used as a sign-off at the end of each section
a duotone treatment applied to all imagery in the brand hue
oversized section openers using the display face at extreme size
a measured scroll-linked progress indicator in the brand hue
palette_strategy: One saturated brand hue used sparingly against warm, tinted neutrals
Deep brand-hue ground for hero and footer, light tinted neutral for content
Monochrome tinted neutrals with the brand hue only on actions and data
Two tones of the brand hue (deep + light) plus one neutral, nothing else
Light, airy tinted ground with a deep ink colour derived from the brand hue
Brand hue as a confident full-bleed field once per page, restrained elsewhere
Tinted dark ground (not near-black) with light type and a single bright brand accent
Neutrals sampled from a material (stone, paper, metal) plus the brand hue
Pure white ground, near-black ink, the brand hue as the only colour (bold, confident, gallery-like)
Photography-led: neutral white/grey UI so commissioned images carry the colour; brand hue on actions only
type_strategy: One superfamily (sans + serif cuts) for total coherence
A grotesque used alone, hierarchy only through weight and size contrast
A characterful serif for display, a neutral grotesque for text
A wide or extended display face with a quiet text face
A humanist sans for warmth plus a sharp text serif for long reading
A condensed display face at heroic sizes plus a generous text face
A modern transitional serif used for everything, including UI
A geometric sans with a distinctive single-storey 'a' or unusual numerals, paired with a mono only for real data
